value.body: A language trainer teaches a foreign language — to school students, college learners, working professionals or staff of companies with overseas clients. Language institutes, private schools, ed-tech platforms and corporate training teams hire trainers, and many teach independently online.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.A. or M.A. in the language with certified proficiency

items.label: Common exams taught
items.value: CEFR levels (DELF, Goethe), JLPT, HSK, DELE

items.label: UG enrolment, Foreign Language
items.note: Undergraduates whose major discipline is a foreign language; not a count of trainers
items.source: AISHE 2023-24 (Ministry of Education), Table 12, actual responses

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Start by teaching beginner-level batches at language institutes or online platforms; a demo class is the usual selection step. Teaching school students in formal posts may also need a B.Ed.

value.title: At a glance
items: Demand follows study-abroad, migration and outsourcing trends.
Pay is often per batch or per hour at the start.
Experienced trainers move into curriculum design or examiner roles.

value.title: Undergraduate enrolment in Foreign Language
value.note: Based on institutions that responded to AISHE each year; AISHE groups all foreign languages together in this table.

competition.note: BA (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among BA (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
women.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
